objectives.text: Keep the Museveni system and hand it on inside the family. Museveni won a seventh term (71.65%, election of 15 Jan 2026, official count as reported) and was sworn in in May 2026. His son Gen. Muhoozi Kainerugaba has been Chief of Defence Forces since March 2024 and announced in August 2026 a bid for the presidency in 2031.

means.text: Two export earners. Gold: declared 2025 gold exports of USD 5.8bn (central bank; USD 3.3bn in 2024), a figure the UN panel puts at USD 6.4bn and above Uganda's own output; 31 t of gold went to the UAE in 2024 (SWISSAID, from UN Comtrade data), and the UN finding ties much of the surplus to gold smuggled from Ituri, DRC. Oil: the EACOP corridor through Tanzania, with the Kingfisher and Tilenga fields as first production, the largest prospective source of export income; 79% complete at end-2025, start-up targeted for 31 July 2026 and first crude from Tanga for October 2026, neither confirmed in sources found. Schedule slippage is the recurrent risk.

paradoxes.text: Operation Shujaa is meant to contain the ADF, yet the UN panel reports (leaked July 2025 report) that Ugandan units expanded their presence in eastern DRC on their own initiative, forming a buffer that shielded M23 from counter-attacks. The 2024 panel had reported active support from some officers; Uganda denies it. The campaign that secures the border feeds the war on the other side of it.

grand_strategy.reading: Uganda's grand strategy is the survival of the Museveni system, now being handed on to Muhoozi, and it pays for that by becoming a regional security power (Juba, Somalia, eastern DRC) and the corridor for Lake Albert oil and for gold. The 2026 election and the 2025 military courts law show a regime that wins at home by control of information and courts while its donors cool (AGOA lost, aid thin). The army is its strength and its trap: each deployment that secures the regime also ties Uganda to the wars on its borders and to the gold trade the UN now traces. Refugees (about two million, largest in Africa) are the regional weight it cannot shed, funded at a fraction of need. Not verified for this card: Israel and Russia (only a 2019 nuclear agreement and a 2025 letter found), the 2025 US aid freeze beyond news reports, Turkey, Saudi Arabia and the Gulf beyond gold, and the Ebola outbreak of 2025.

stances.note: Kampala says the UPDF deployed to save Kiir and Juba (March 2025); Juba acknowledged technical and support units under a pre-existing military pact (a tier 4 pointer). No alliance treaty was found, so the grade is de facto alignment with a client. No source uses the word ally: the grade is our reading of the structure (C). Bond none, not affinity: the motive Kampala gives is regime protection, and no source names kinship or affinity. The SSD card reads the same alignment from its side as ally; the grade here is Uganda's own view.

stances.note: Kinshasa agreed to Operation Shujaa with the UPDF from November 2021, so the two cooperate against the ADF out of necessity. Uganda resists alignment: the ICJ ordered it to pay USD 325m in reparations for its 1998-2003 occupation (judgment of 9 February 2022, payable in five USD 65m instalments; the first was paid in September 2022). Later instalments, due to 1 September 2026, are not verified. The UN experts say Ugandan units shielded M23 (July 2025 report as reported); Uganda denies it. reluctant_partner is our reading of that structure, not a source's word. Bond grievance: the ICJ case is an open wound. Gap: whether the 2026 instalments were paid.

stances.note: Rwanda shut the Gatuna/Katuna crossing in February 2019; the 2020 summit produced an extradition deal and the crossing reopened in 2022, with Muhoozi as Museveni's envoy (Al Jazeera, March 2022, 'to fix relations'). Since 2025 the military channel has warmed: Muhoozi met Kagame in March 2025, commanders met in October 2025, and Muhoozi was in Kigali in July 2026. Warming and reluctant are our reading (C); no source uses the words. Bond grievance: the 2019 standoff and the security disputes left open. Gap: trade and movement at Gatuna are not confirmed; the 2026 coverage is mostly Rwandan official or state-aligned, so the picture is one-sided.
